items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: And we got to be great friends throughout our lives, the kid and I.

ctx.x: No. I know. My mother married very big on race. Oh my God. You didn’t screw around with blacks. Because when I was in nursery school, she would take me to nursery school and the very next year my brother to nursery school, we were in a little housing thing. My father was off in World War II. And it was me, and this little other guy who was black, and my mother held my hand and his hand. And then two days a week the lady — right now I’m trying to remember the names, we were so close — would hold my hand and his…
A boy? A black boy also?
